newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Holiday sales key focus.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Holiday sales key focus.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries are expected to continue their upward trend Tuesday, but activity is seen slowing as the market looks ahead to Thanksgiving.
"(Monday) was fairly active, which could suggest people getting things out of the way" ahead of the holiday, said Marty Mauro, senior economist at Merrill Lynch & Co.
On the final full day of trading this week, pre-holiday shopping sales figures will influence trading most, analysts said.
Due at 0900 EST/1400 GMT is the Bank of Tokyo- Mitsubishi/Schroder Wertheim chain store sales report for the week ended November 23.
An hour later, the Conference Board will release its October consumer confidence report and at 1455 EST/1955 GMT, the Redbook Research retail sales survey is due.

With the market confident the Federal Reserve will not be playing Scrooge and raising interest rates in December, attention shifts to spending data now that the holiday shopping season is in full swing.

But it will take very strong numbers to rattle the bond market, players said. All the recent economic indicators point to a slowing, most recently, Monday's 1.5 percent drop in October existing home sales.
"People don't want to sell," said a trader at a Japanese-owned primary dealership. "We haven't had retail customers sell in weeks and there's nothing this week that will cause them to sell."
In addition to friendly fundamentals, technicals are strong as well, market participants said.
A key variable is how the slower trading volume will affect the market. Traders are bracing for the possibility of sharp swings, given the lack of liquidity this time of year.
Meanwhile, some noted that, with the Fed expected to buy coupons in the near future -- most likely after Thanksgiving -- the market should retain its underlying good tone.
Monday, the 30-year bond was up 8/32 at 101-1/32 to yield 6.42 percent. The two-year note was 1/32 higher at 99-19/32 to yield 5.68 percent.
Fed funds are expected to open between the 5-1/4 percent target rate and 5-5/16 percent.
